content: 1. Co-administration of certain drugs, such as remimazolam with opioid analgesics or sedative/hypnotics, can lead to profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or even death. It is essential to continuously monitor the patient’s vital signs during sedation and the recovery period. The dosage of remimazolam should be carefully titrated when used with these agents. 2. Doxylamine increases the effects of rimabotulinumtoxin B due to pharmacodynamic synergy. Drugs with anticholinergic effects may enhance the effects of botulinum toxin, potentially causing excessive neuromuscular weakness and systemic anticholinergic effects. Close monitoring is advised. 3. Doxylamine and risperidone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Roxithromycin decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Doxylamine and sage both increase sedation. The significance of this interaction is unknown, but close monitoring is recommended. 6. Doxylamine and skullcap both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Selinexor and pyridoxine have an unspecified interaction mechanism. Patients treated with selinexor may experience neurological toxicities. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 8. Selinexor and doxylamine have an unspecified interaction mechanism. Co-administration may increase the risk of dizziness or confusion. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 9. Sevoflurane and doxylamine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Doxylamine and shepherd’s purse both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Siberian ginseng increases the effects of doxylamine through pharmacodynamic synergy. This may enhance central nervous system (CNS) depression. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 12. Doxylamine and sodium oxybate both increase the effects of each other through pharmacodynamic synergy. Co-administration may result in profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or death. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If co-administration is unavoidable, limit dosages and durations to the minimum required and monitor closely for signs of respiratory depression and sedation. 13. Stiripentol and doxylamine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Concomitant use of stiripentol with other CNS depressants, including alcohol, may increase the risk of sedation and somnolence. 14. Streptomycin decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 15. Doxylamine and sufentanil both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of sufentanil and doxylamine may result in hypotension, profound sedation, respiratory depression, coma, or death. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 16. Sulfadiazine decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 17. Sulfamethoxazole decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 18. Sulfisoxazole decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 19. Doxylamine and tapentadol both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Teicoplanin decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 21. Temazepam and doxylamine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Temocillin decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 23. Tetracycline decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 24. Theophylline decreases levels of pyridoxine by altering metabolism. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 25. Doxylamine and thioridazine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Doxylamine and thiothixene both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Tigecycline decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 28. Tobramycin decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 29. Doxylamine and topiramate both increase sedation. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 30. Doxylamine and tramadol both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Tranylcypromine increases the effects of doxylamine through an unspecified mechanism. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Tranylcypromine should not be administered with antihistamines due to potential additive CNS depressant effects. MAO inhibitors also prolong and intensify the anticholinergic effects of antihistamines. 32. Doxylamine and trazodone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Doxylamine and triazolam both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Doxylamine and triclofos both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Doxylamine and trifluoperazine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Trimethoprim decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 37. Doxylamine and trimipramine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Triprolidine and doxylamine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Valerian increases the effects of doxylamine through pharmacodynamic synergy. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration of valerian and doxylamine may result in increased sedation. Avoid or use alternative drugs. 40. Vancomycin decreases the level or effect of pyridoxine by altering intestinal flora. This interaction applies only to the oral forms of both agents. The significance of this interaction is unknown. 41. Doxylamine increases sedation, while xylometazoline decreases sedation. The effect of this interaction is unclear; use caution. 42. Doxylamine and ziconotide both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Doxylamine and ziprasidone both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Doxylamine and zotepine both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Doxylamine and zuranolone both increase the effects of each other through pharmacodynamic synergy. Co-administration may increase impairment of psychomotor performance or CNS depressant effects. Avoid or use alternative drugs. If unavoidable, consider dose reduction. 46. Common adverse effects of doxylamine include somnolence, dizziness, headache, blurred vision, dry mouth, and gastrointestinal disturbances such as constipation or diarrhea. Anticholinergic effects may exacerbate conditions like asthma, glaucoma, or urinary retention. 47. Doxylamine is intended for the treatment of nausea and vomiting during pregnancy in women who do not respond to conservative management. Epidemiologic studies have not reported an increased risk of congenital malformations. 48. Women should not breastfeed while on doxylamine therapy, as the drug can pass into breast milk and may cause sedation, irritability, or respiratory issues in nursing infants. 49. Pyridoxine hydrochloride is excreted into breast milk, and adverse events in infants exposed through breastfeeding have been reported. 50. Doxylamine should be taken on an empty stomach with water, as food delays its onset of action and lowers peak levels. The tablet should be swallowed whole without chewing, crushing, or splitting.
